question.prompt: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.
expectedPoints: Sort intervals primarily by start time
Iterate through sorted intervals and compare current start with previous end
Update previous end using max(previous.end, current.end)
State O(N log N) time complexity due to sorting and O(N) space for output
commonMistakes: Attempting to merge without sorting first
Failing when current interval is completely enclosed in previous interval

transcript: Candidate: First, we cannot assume the intervals are sorted, so we must sort them by their start time. That takes O(N log N) time. After sorting, we initialize an output list with the first interval. Then we iterate through the remaining intervals. If the current interval's start is less than or equal to the last merged interval's end, they overlap, so we merge them by setting the end to the maximum of both ends. Otherwise, there is no overlap, so we append the current interval to our output. Space complexity is O(N) to store the merged intervals. For testing, I would test [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]] which merges to [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]].
notes: Solid standard textbook solution. Well explained. Testing only covered the happy path example from prompt, did not check empty array or nested intervals.
